candidates.summary: every screenshot is republished at a byte-identical URL on each push, so the sticky comment's before/after can show the previous push
candidates.failure_scenario: name := slug(strings.TrimPrefix(urlOf(r), "/")) makes the shot filename a pure function of the realm path, and the publish job writes it under a per-PR directory (pr-preview-publish.yml:138-140, "rm -rf pr-$PR; mkdir -p pr-$PR; cp -r ../_preview/.") on a site whose base URL carries no sha. The comment is then PATCHed in place (pr-preview-publish.yml:174, gh api -X PATCH .../issues/comments/$id). Push twice to a pull request that changes a realm's render: the second render writes new bytes at exactly https:///pr-6194/_shots/r-gnoland-home--after.png, the comment body is edited to the identical , and GitHub's image proxy answers from its cache for that URL. The reviewer reads a before/after that belongs to the previous head, with nothing in the comment saying so.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n 'name := slug' misc/gnopreview/shots.go and grep -n 'gh api -X PATCH' .github/workflows/pr-preview-publish.yml -- confirms the URL is stable across pushes and the comment is edited rather than replaced (both run). Then the live half: push twice to a PR inside the cache window and compare the image GitHub renders against _preview/_shots/*.png, or curl -I the published PNG on gnolang.github.io and read its Cache-Control.
candidates.evidence: shots.go:85 `name := slug(strings.TrimPrefix(urlOf(r), "/"))`; shots.go:88 writes `name+"-after.png"`; pr-preview-publish.yml:110 `Concurrent pull requests share one branch, each owning only its own pr-/`; pr-preview-publish.yml:174 `gh api -X PATCH "repos/$REPO/issues/comments/$id" -F body=@_preview/comment.md`. No query string or content hash anywhere in comment.go's img src (``, comment.go:113-122).

candidates.summary: the _before/ tree is published with no link to it anywhere, though the README says it exists so a reviewer can click through to the before page
candidates.failure_scenario: README.md:73-74 says `_before/` is written "so a reviewer can click through to the before page and not just its screenshot". ShotPair carries one page URL and shots.go:86 fills it with the AFTER page only (`URL: path.Dir(afterFile) + "/"`); comment.go:117-119 renders the before cell as a bare `` while only the after image is wrapped in ``; Index() iterates p.Realms against the head crawler, so no _before entry appears there either. A reviewer who wants to read the before page's text -- the case where the 1280x860 shot crops what changed -- has no link and no documented path, and the published snapshot carries a whole render tree nothing can reach.
